newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Red October confectioner raising output to 72,000T.
newsitem.headline: Red October confectioner raising output to 72,000T.

text.p: Russia's biggest confectioner AO Red October plans to raise its 1997 output to 72,000 tonnes from 58,000 tonnes in 1996, Interfax news agency quoted the company's president Anatoly Daursky as saying on Friday.

Daursky told Interfax that the rise would be due to the start of production at the company's new factory in Kolomna, with an annual capacity of 7,500 tonnes. The start of production in Kolomna is planned for May.
AOOT Moskovskaya Konditerskaya Fabrika Krasny Oktyabr (Red October) plans to issue preferred shares and a Eurobond soon to finance production in Kolomna.
A factory in Ryazan, 97-percent owned by Red October, plans to raise its production by over 6,000 tonnes to 12,500 tonnes in 1997, Daursky was quoted by Interfax as saying.
He said 75 percent of Red October's production was sold in Moscow and 15 percent are exported.
